Where it began

Shaheen Shah Afridi was born in Landi Kotal, in Khyber District, on 6 April 2000, and grew up there as the youngest of seven brothers. His first cricket was played on the Tatara Ground, which takes its name from the hills close by, and until 2015 he had only ever bowled with a tennis ball.

The man who changed that was his eldest brother, Riaz Afridi, who had played a Test for Pakistan in 2004. Riaz brought him to the FATA Under-16 trials that year and put a hard ball in his hand. By November 2015 he was touring Australia with the Pakistan Under-16 side.

The player

He arrived in a hurry. Playing his first first-class match, for Khan Research Laboratories in September 2017, he took 8 for 39 in the second innings, the best figures by a Pakistani on first-class debut at the time. His Test debut followed against New Zealand on 3 December 2018, and a year later he took his first five-wicket haul in Tests, against Sri Lanka.

His finest Test came in the West Indies in August 2021. He took 10 for 94 in the second Test, was named Player of the Match, and Pakistan levelled the series. By November 2026 he had played 34 Tests and taken 126 wickets at 28.13, with four five-wicket innings and a best of 6 for 51.

What made him special

Height, pace, the angle from left arm and good control were the gifts people noticed early. With the new ball he swung it into the batter, and with the old one he could make it reverse. In October 2025 he used that reverse swing to take four wickets in the final innings against South Africa, and Pakistan won the Test by 93 runs. In December 2021 he climbed into the ICC's top five Test bowlers, the youngest fast bowler in the world to be there at that time.

His batting was a quieter matter. Nobody picked him for it, and 269 Test runs at 7.27 explain why, though a top score of 29 not out shows he could hang around when the mood took him.

Away from the middle

In January 2022 the ICC named him its Men's Cricketer of the Year for 2021. He was the first Pakistani to receive the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy, after a year in which he took 78 wickets in 36 internationals.

He was a leader too. As captain of Lahore Qalandars he won the Pakistan Super League in 2022, 2023 and 2025, the first captain to win it three times, and he even designed the team's new kit for the 2023 season. In October 2025 he was made Pakistan's ODI captain, and he soon led them to their first home one-day series win over South Africa.

And finally

Until 2015 he had never bowled with a hard ball. Six years later the ICC called him the best cricketer of the year. Whatever they teach on the tennis-ball pitches of Landi Kotal, it seems to work.
